description: Weighted scientific rubric for the behaviour x hyperbolic RQ-VAE mechanism selection (Issue #122). Weights are a policy, not a score: change them before a new round starts, never halfway through one.

dimensions.name: behavior_evidence
dimensions.five_of_five: A concrete training-only behavioural failure or problem with auditable coverage and support, and a specific SID hypothesis about it

anchors.0: no behavioural problem is named, or the named one is contradicted by the data contract
anchors.1: unsupported speculation about a behavioural problem
anchors.2: a vague behavioural claim, or one whose evidence is high-risk and not measured
anchors.3: a plausible, testable behavioural problem with a stated statistic
anchors.4: a well-supported behavioural problem with a measured statistic and its coverage
anchors.5: a strongly supported problem: the statistic is measured, its support and coverage are auditable, and the SID hypothesis follows from it

dimensions.name: geometry_necessity
dimensions.five_of_five: A genuine curved computation with a credible reason it contributes beyond an appropriately matched Euclidean control

anchors.0: no curved operation, or the geometry is inherited and unused
anchors.1: a geometry name without a geometric computation
anchors.2: a curved operation that a matched Euclidean transform could reproduce
anchors.3: a curved operation that plausibly does something the Euclidean control cannot
anchors.4: a curved operation whose added value is argued against a matched control
anchors.5: a curved operation whose necessity is argued, whose matched Euclidean counterpart is specified, and whose cancellations are ruled out

dimensions.name: novelty
dimensions.five_of_five: Distinct computation against the cited literature and the actual experiment ledger, not a rename or a routine loss variation

anchors.0: identical to a mechanism already measured here
anchors.1: a rename of an existing mechanism
anchors.2: a routine variation of an existing mechanism
anchors.3: a distinct computation relative to the cited work
anchors.4: distinct and argued against the cited work and our own ledger
anchors.5: distinct, argued against cited work and our ledger, with the prior art traceable and the difference computational

dimensions.name: downstream_mechanism
dimensions.five_of_five: An explicit causal chain from the changed code assignment or representation to next-item recommendation, with a measurable expected effect

anchors.0: no chain from the mechanism to recommendation
anchors.1: a hoped-for effect with no mechanism
anchors.2: a hand-waved chain with a gap
anchors.3: a plausible chain with a measurable effect
anchors.4: a specific chain with the assignment change and the expected effect named
anchors.5: a specific chain, the affected assignment, the observable and the expected direction, each with a diagnostic

dimensions.name: falsifiability
dimensions.five_of_five: Clean behaviour-off, geometry-off (matched Euclidean) and both-on controls, failure criteria and discriminating diagnostics

anchors.0: no controls and no failure criterion
anchors.2: controls that differ in more than the intended switch
anchors.3: three controls and a failure criterion
anchors.4: three matched controls, a failure criterion and a discriminating diagnostic
anchors.5: three matched controls, a falsifier, a discriminating diagnostic, and a statement of what would refute the mechanism

dimensions.name: implementability
dimensions.five_of_five: Correct, differentiable, numerically guarded and practical under the frozen training budget, with specific repairable risks noted

anchors.1: missing the specification needed to implement it
anchors.2: implementable only with an unspecified redesign
anchors.5: implementable, differentiable, numerically guarded, affordable in the frozen budget, with the remaining risks named

dimensions.name: exploration_value
dimensions.five_of_five: Addresses a substantially different mechanism or failure mode and teaches something even if Stage 3 is negative

anchors.0: repeats a measured negative in the same family
anchors.1: a near-repeat of a measured mechanism
anchors.2: a small variation of a measured mechanism
anchors.3: a different mechanism or failure mode
anchors.4: a substantially different mechanism with a clear lesson if it fails
anchors.5: a substantially different mechanism or failure mode whose negative result would be informative on its own
